Deed of sale of a part of a house. In the hand of Yosef b. Shemuel ha-Levi. Location: Fustat. Dated: 1514 Seleucid = 1202/03 CE. Names: Abū l-Riḍā al-Levi al-ʿAttar, [... b.] Tamīm ha-Levi, Sitt al-Karam bt. Abū Saʿīd al-Levi al-Tājir, Shemuel ha-Talmid b. [...]. Sitt al-Karam evidently sells the quarter of the house which she owns. AA. ASE.
Minute fragment from a letter: ומגאראתך עלי . . . תסלם עליך . . .
Small fragment of accounts in Judaeo-Arabic. Probably in the hand of Abū Zikrī Kohen.
Accounts. (Information from CUDL)

Letter/petition from two men addressed to a dignitary. Refers to Sunday the 8th of Ṭevet. Dating: Probably 12th century. On recto there is a vocalized qaddish. (Information from Goitein's index card.) There are some odd-looking words such as ואלנאורציה and סקאטף.

Commercial accounts in Judaeo-Arabic. Dating: likely ca. 12th century. Mentions items such as coral and silk and kerchiefs and rhubarb. May mention the name R. Simḥa and the name בן זרוק. There are some Arabic-script jottings as well.
Likely a medical prescription.

Bill of divorce (geṭ). Location: Fusṭāṭ. Dated: 2 Sivan 1395 Seleucid, which is 9 May 1084 CE. Husband: Kathīr b. Yehoshuaʿ. Wife: Mawʿā bt. Moshe. Signed by: Aharon b. Avraham; Eliyahhu b. [...]. No documentation of receipt on verso. (Information from Goitein's index card and CUDL)

Phrases from a letter addressed to a Jewish notable: מרדכ]י הזמן ראש מערכות ישראל . . . ירום הודו וירבה כבודו . . . ממשלתו בן כבוד גדולת קדו . . . 

Qadish on verso.
Accounts in Judaeo-Arabic on recto and verso. In the hand of ʿArūs b. Yosef. Mentions a wakīl and Yosef and lac and tartar
Legal fragment (lower right corner). Signed: [...] b. Yosef ha-Kohen; Shela b. Mevasser (dated documents 1065–1103). On verso there is a prescription/recipe in Arabic script.

Bifolio from a court notebook. 

Right page: a summons written by Yefet b. David the cantor, summoning Neḥemya b. Avraham to court due to complaints against him filed by Avraham b. Shemuel ha-Levi. Dated: Thursday, 10 Tammuz 1343 Seleucid = 22 June 1032 CE. 

Left page: see separate PGP record.

On verso there are seliḥot (right page) and talmudic writings (left page). (Information in part from E. Bareket, Shafrir Misrayim, pp.138, 167, 169, 252)

Small fragment of a legal document in Arabic script involving [...] b. Hārūn al-Yahūdī (and?) a supplier to the mint ([mū]rid bi-dār al-ḍarb). There are a few words in Judaeo-Arabic in the upper margin.

Deed of acknowledgment (iqrār). In Arabic script. Damaged with the imprint of another document on top of it. Needs examination for content. On verso there is the imprint of what is probably an Ottoman-era legal document involving Abū ʿImrān Mūsā b. [...] al-faqīr ilā Allāh and Muḥammad al-[...] al-Shāfiʿī. Written in giant letters: "the 23rd of the month of."
Fragmentary letter mentioning several names and a parnas.

Fragment from a letter/petition from Abū Saʿīd Ibn al-Muʿallima to Maḍmūn b. [Ḥasan] the Nagid of Yemen. In Judaeo-Arabic, with long introductory formulae in Hebrew. Of note one of Maḍmūn's titles here is מרדכי הזמן, which later became typical of Maimonides' titles, but was not unique to him. The sender is a teacher in the Iraqi synagogue (מע]לם בכניסה אל[ער]אקיין) and also mentions a certain Shelomo [...] al-ḥaver. The continuation and almost all of the substance are missing. Likely he goes on to ask for financial support for the synagogue/community, as we find in other letters sent from Fust
Verso: Fatimid decree fragment. Three words preserved. (MR)
Fragment of a letter in Arabic script.

Legal document in which a paternal cousin (al-shaykh al-mukram al-Kohen Pinḥas) of a man’s wife (bint al-Muṣinn) renounces his inheritance rights on one-fourth of a house belonging to her against ten dinars promised to him by her husband (Abu Naṣr al-ʿAṭṭār known as Ibn Khalaf Ḥawājib) in case she precedes him in death. Dated: Sunday, 5 Ṭevet 1554 = 30 November 1242 CE. Unsigned, but mentions Yosef as a witness. (Information from Goitein's index cards and Mediterranean Society, 4:279) EMS
Small fragment of a letter. Containing greetings "to you and to your family (ahl baytak)."

Bifolio from a notebook with accounts and drafts. In Judaeo-Arabic and Arabic script. Entries are arranged by the parsha of the week. Mentions al-Shaykh al-Rashīd Bū l-Faḍl. (Information in part from CUDL)
Syriac pre-Anaphora rite with rubrics in Garshuni. Information from Kiraz, "Learning Syriac and Garshuni in Early Modern Egypt."
Accounts in Judaeo-Arabic. Mentions people such as al-Rayyis Abū l-Faḍl, the mother of al-Rayyis Abū Manṣūr, Abū l-Faraj Ṣabbāgh, and Abū l-Ṭāhir Ḥarīrī.

Fragment of a legal document. Cryptic phrases about "releasing myself from God" and "the vicissitudes of time" and saying to a woman "you will regret. . ." Might be related to the neighboring fragments (similar state of discoloration).
Accounts in Judaeo-Arabic in the hand of ʿArūs b. Yosef. Mentions Barakāt b. Khulayf.
Judaeo-Arabic love poetry.
Minute fragment from the top of a legal document. Involving Manṣūr b. Zikrī b. Yūsuf and Wafāʾ b. S[...].
Accounts of some sort. Possibly from the ill-defined genre tentatively called 'commercial receipts' on PGP—see tag. Needs examination.
Calendar or ephemeris in Arabic script. Lists entries for the days of the week along with corresponding celestial objects.
Commercial letter mentioning Abū Saʿd. Small fragment, little of the content is preserved. (Information from CUDL)
Magical or esoteric text. Mainly in Hebrew and Aramaic.
Accounts, probably related to: T-S Ar.34.130 (PGPID 20505).

Ketubba fragment. Dated: Ḥeshvan 136[.] Seleucid, corresponding to the range 1048–57 CE. For the remarriage of a previously divorced couple. Bride: [...] bt. Sahl. (Information from Goitein's index card.)

IB IV, 41 (ח55). Letter from Yiṣḥaq b. Avraham Ibn ʿEzra, in Spain, to Ḥalfon b. Netanel ha-Levi. In Judaeo-Arabic. Dating: after 1 Nisan 1139 CE. 

r11–12 and v5 contain Coptic numerals used as a code, presumably substituting for Hebrew letters, but with a substitution mechanism that has not yet been determined. (MR)

The Coptic numerals on the verso are doubtful. MAF suggests 1, 60, 100, 400, 40, 1, 100, 1, ?, 8, 8. What he identifies as 1s (𐋡) look more like 4s (𐋤). The one he marks as 60 (𐋯) is doubtful. The one he marks as doubtful might be 900 (𐋻). (PG)
Legal query to Hodayahu ha-Nasi. See parallel in ENA 4045.19 (PGPID 15920).

Opening of a letter from Yaʿaqov b. Elʿazar al-Dijwār (דגואר) to Avraham Maimonides (r. 1205–1237 CE). The same person also appears in T-S 8J23.2 (PGPID 7699), a letter from Peraḥya b. Yosef. None of the content is preserved. AA

Verso: Fragment from near the beginning of a state document in Arabic script. Mainly preserving blessings for someone powerful (وصيانته ومراعاته وحراسته . . . وحماية(؟) . . . وفيض الابدي . . . ). Huge letters, chancery hand, wide space between the lines.

Recto: Probably a medical prescription. Ends "nāfiʿ mubārak."

Verso: Possibly a line from a state document in Arabic script. The same line has been copied twice.

Contract in which Ṣedaqa b. Muvḥar, a scholar known from a number of manuscripts dating to 1076–86 CE (e.g. T-S 20.110 (PGPID 1774)) gives 50 dinars to his elder daughter Sitt al-Aqrān Mufaddāt and 25 dinars to his younger daughter Sitt al-Yumn Taqiyya. In the scribal hand of Hillel b. ʿEli (fl. 1066–1108 CE). The money is destined for their trousseaus when they reach maturity, but will in the meantime be supervised by the oil merchant (zayyāt) Abū Manṣūr Aharon b. Mevasser in the form of a partnership to which Aharon himself contributes the small sum of 5 dinars. The total capital of 80 dinar

Accounts in Arabic script. The hand is reminiscent of fiscal documents but these may be private accounts, based on the unsystematic layout and the headers "owed by him" (ʿalayhi).Recto mentionsn "on Wednesday the 26th" followed by "20 dinars," then perhaps "in the hand of Jaʿfar al-[...]. Entries on verso mention 40 raṭls of something followed by term muqāṭaʿa; underneath possibly 400-something units of wood (ʿūd) again followed by muqāṭaʿa. Merits further examination.

Recto: copy of a legal document, concerned with marital arrangements (for example the husband will not forbid his wife to visit her mother and brother). Verso: list of names such as Abū l-Khayr, Ibn Saʿd and Abū [...]. (Information from CUDL)
Legal document. Small fragment (lower right corner). Dated: Tishrei 1484 Seleucid = September/October 1172 CE, under the authority of the Gaʾon (probably Sar Shalom ha-Levi).

Legal document. Fragment (bottom part). In the hand of Ḥalfon b. Menashshe. Involves Berakhot and Ḥasān(?). Dated: 1442 Seleucid, which is 1130/31 CE, under the authority of Maṣliaḥ Gaʾon. (Information from CUDL)

Letter in Hebrew by the muqaddam (head) of the community of Minyat Zifta, announcing that he had excommunicated a debtor according to an instruction by the Nagid. The Nagid had previously arranged for the debtor to repay part of what was owed to his creditors, but he reneged on his agreement and an excommunication was about to be enacted against him as per the Nagid’s instructions. The muqaddam, however, asks for a respite of one or two months for the debtor. Ca. 14th century. (Information from Mediterranean Society, I, 465 and CUDL)
Order of payment in Arabic script. The judge (al-dayyān) is asked to pay a sum to the bearer. See T-S AS 179.212 (PGPID 36725) and the related orders listed there.

Small fragment from a legal deed regarding a passageway belonging to Efrayim the elder and his wife (?). Written by Halfon b. Menashshe ha-Levi (1100–38 CE). T-S NS 190.78 (PGPID 23888) and T-S NS 224.23 (PGPID 24019) might be an indirect join.
A few words in large Arabic script: al-mawlā al-shaykh al-makhdūm. State document? There are also several Hebrew literary texts on this fragment.
Literary. Epistle from Plato to Porphyry. In Judaeo-Arabic. On asceticism.
Monograph; probably from a formulary of legal documents (or related discussion), including the passage: ואלב׳ אגראצ׳א תכתץ בהא אלשמושין דון גירהא...   (Data from FGP)
Fol. 3: Possibly a replacement ketubba (אורכתא). Mentions Aharon. Signed by Yoshiyyahu b. ʿAmram.

Petition or report or draft of one, in Arabic script. Strings of titles. There are alternating lines of light ink (bigger letters) and dark ink (smaller letters). The text in the bigger script is mostly faded and blotted.
Letter in Hebrew and Judaeo-Arabic. Mentions Zayn al-Tujjār and Rabbenu Nahray Gadol ha-Yeshiva (=Nahray b. Nissim?). The sender's name may be Yosef (there is a very faded address on verso).
Fragment of a letter from a child to a father ("yā wālidī"). May mention a meeting with a cantor (la-qad ijtamaʿa al-ḥazzān....) and mentions pounds of meat (arṭāl laḥm...).
Table of phrases in Arabic script, probably for purposes of divination/prognosticating. Needs examination.
Monograph; from Saadias formulary of legal documents (near end); published by Ben-Sasson in Shenaton Hamishpat Ha-Ivri. (Info from FGP)

On bottom of f. 2r are accounts or a list mentioning precious and base metals including silver, red arsenic, and mercury in Arabic script. F. 1r and 2v: collection of piyyuṭim on the story of Joseph in Genesis 44. F. 1r contains a midraš from a qerova of Yannai to the seder ויגש אליו יהודה. It is followed by the first 8 lines of the yoṣer אח מכרתם בנעלים by Solomon b. Sulaymān (Zulay: by Pinḥas ha-Kohen), the final four of which are added in a different hand. F. 2v contains 2 piyyuṭim including the qerova מרגלים אתם שמעו ונבהלו by Simeon b. Megas. F. 1v: explanation of the ṣiṣit, which are com
Accounts in Judaeo-Arabic on recto and verso, all in a very difficult scribal hand. Medieval-era. Requires further examination.

Fragment of a ketubba. Bride: [...] bt. Yoel b. Yeshuʿa. Groom: Shelomo b. [...]. Location: Fusṭāṭ. Dating: ca. 1237–79 CE, as it is written In the hand of ʿImmanuel b. Yeḥiel (active ca. 1231–79), under the authority of David I Maimonides (in office ca. 1237–1300). (Information from CUDL and Goitein's index card.)
Legal document relating to a ketubba (trousseau list), mentioning the groom [...] son of the late [...] ha-Levi ha-Parnas and the bride Mubāraka. (Information from CUDL)
Recto: letter or note, in the hand of Avraham Maimonides. Verso: Arabic jottings maybe mentioning al-Asyūṭī. (Information in part from CUDL)
Long strip of paper with only a few words, possibly legal formularies (פלן בן...). Requires further examination. AA/MCD

Petition addressed to the Fatimid caliph based on the raʿy clause towards the end "wa li-mawlāna ṣalawāt Allah ʿalayhi ʿāliya al-raʾy". In a rudimentary or sloppy chancery hand. The beginnings of 12 lines are preserved. At the top: "... al-aʾimma al-ṭāhirīn wa-abnāʾih al-akramīn. Wa-l-ʿabd...." The petitioner asks for an edict to be issued "to the chief judge to investigate" (ilā qāḍī al-quḍāt bi l-kashf) in line 9. In the next line: "... baynahum li-yataḥaqqaq bi-dhālik..." Needs examination. 

Reused on the same side for Hebrew pen trials (including the name Moshe b. Yiṣḥaq he-Ḥaver and a

Recto is a literary text in Arabic in red and blank ink, vocalized and beautifully written.

Verso is an account in Arabic, maybe of collaterals (رهن appears at upper right).

Recto: part of a copy of a replacement ketubba for ʿAzīza bt. [...] and Saʿīd b. Yiṣḥaq. Dated: 5294 AM = 1533/34 CE. Location: Cairo. The original ketubba had been lost. Lower part of document not preserved, including any names of witnesses. 

Verso: (a) two drafts or templates of legal documents (one in Judaeo-Arabic and one in Hebrew) in which a wife promises not to insult her husband, etc. (b) the end of a letter or query involving Esther, rumors, R. Yishmaʿel, and R. Yehuda אבורכיל. (Information in part from CUDL and Goitein's index card.)

Bifolio of accounts. Two of the four pages have Judaeo-Arabic accounting in a rudimentary hand. These mention Ibn Ghulayb; Ibn Saʿadya; Ibn al-Dhahabī.

One of the pages contains Arabic accounting in an elegant hand. Mentions: al-Rāsila(?); the rent of an animal; al-ḥazzān; the camel (driver, presumably) Sualyamān; cotton; soap; the officer of estates (rājil al-mawārīth). And sums including 47, 21, and 70 or 90 dirhams from Abū l-Ḥasan ʿAllūn.

Court record. Mentions a woman who died and a dispute over an inheritance involving Abū Isḥāq Yoshiyya (the same as in T-S 12.37 (PGPID 3143)?), "the children," and ʿEli. The bottom two lines are intriguing: "the Byzantines blocked the road before us (פקטעו אלרום עלינא אלטריק). . . and I put it in my belt (al-himyān). . . ." (Information in part from CUDL)
Legal document in the hand of Ḥalfon b. Menashshe. Dated: 1435 Seleucid, which is 1123/24 CE. Essentially nothing else preserved.

Court notebook in the hand of Ḥalfon b. Menashshe ha-Levi. 

Fol. 2v: Three entries. Location: Fustat. All dated Tuesday, 17 Tammuz 1438 Seleucid = 28 June 1127 CE.

(1) Malīḥa bt. Abū l-Faḍl the wife of Adam al-Ḥalabī al-Ṣayrafī appoints Natan b. Avraham ha-Levi in order to sue her husband. The witnesses were Berakhot ha-Kohen he-Ḥaver and the cantor Abū l-Ḥasan Ibn al-Kāmanī(?).

(2) The physician (ṭabīb) Abū Naṣr b. Abū l-Ḥasan al-Tinnīsī(?) appoints Abū l-Ḥasan ʿAlī b. Yiṣḥaq al-Kohen known as Ibn Ghazāl to represent him in all his claims against Abū Naṣr b. Abū Saʿīd al-ʿAṭṭār.

Power of attorney. Location: Fustat. Dated: 4976 AM, which is 1215/16 CE, under the reshut of Avraham Maimonides. In which the daughter of Menaḥem ha-Talmid b. Menashshe appoints her husband Sulaymān/Shelomo b. ʿAmram ha-Levi for some purpose (not preserved). (Information from Goitein's index card.)

Legal document written and signed by Ḥalfon b. Menashshe ha-Levi (1100–38), under the authority of Maṣliaḥ Gaʾon (1127–39). Fragment (bottom part). Involves Yaḥyā al-Kohen, Abū l-Maʿālī, Abū l-Karam b. Saʿdān, Abū l-Ḥasan, payment in installments. Probably the same case and parties as in T-S 16.51 (PGPID 7369).

tags: Shemuel b. Hofni, 10th c, learning, lost fragment, travels
desc: Letter from Naḥum b. Yosef al-Baradānī (Qayrawan) to his master Shemuel b. Ḥofni gaon; 7 August 999. The sender, whose family is in Iraq, has been travelling for a long time for an unnamed unpleasant reason. Qayrawan and al-Mahdiyya are among the places that he visited. The writer asks for forgiveness for writing the letter in Arabic (rather than in Hebrew) which was easier for him since he was writing in a hurry. Mentions Shemuel b. Ḥofni’s earlier letter about a difficult situation in Baghdad. Mentions a number of deaths in his family. Asks Shemuel b. Ḥofni to make sure that a certain Abū Ma
A few words from a large state document ([...] min jiha. . .)

State document in Arabic, two lines are visible. Fatimid-era. There is also a remnant of an Arabic text on recto mentioning "Isrāʾīl ʿalayhi al-salām," probably unrelated. This is probably the end of T-S Ar.38.128 + T-S Ar.42.195 (PGPID 39060) (indirect join). Requires further examination.
Family letter. Likely the hand of Abū Sahl Levi (d. 1211). Mentioning Abū l-Ḥasan (Yedutun) and Mūsā/Moshe, who departed when he was sick. (Information in part from CUDL)

Gzar-dina de-Yeshu (Toledot Yeshu, Ar1 in Bohak's edition, "Pilate" recension), containing passages 5.4–9.2, followed by a short Judaeo–Arabic text titled אסמ֯א֯ א֯לטיור אלתי פי ויהי ב[יום] , ‘The names of the birds which are (listed) in (the Torah pericope) “And it was on [the (eighth) day]” (i.e., Lev. 9.1ff)’ and consisting of Saadiah Gaon’s translation of Lev. 11.13–19.15–16 and an Aramaic discussion of shofar-blowing. (Information from Gideon Bohak, The Sentencing of Jesus (Gzar-dina de-Yeshu), 7–8).

NB: Much of Bohak's edition is only legible via multispectral imaging. In his edition
Informal note mentioning Abū Saʿd Ibn al-Kāzarūnī and quires (kurrāsa/kurrāsāt).

Legal document. Probably a release. Fragment (left half only). In Hebrew. Dated: 52[..] AM, which is 1439–1539 CE. Involves [...] Suʿūd known as Ibn ʿIjala and his two brothers; Mardūk known as Ṭūzī; and David. Of the witness signatures only the name "Shaʿra" is preserved, probably someone from the Ibn Shaʿra family.
Recto: part of a letter, mentioning the elder Abū l-[...]. Verso: Letter in Arabic script, probably mercantile mentioning a weight measure, "تخليت عني بوزن". (Information partly from CUDL).
Business accounts in Judaeo-Arabic. Dating: 11th or 12th century. Hand of ʿArūs b. Yosef. Mentions pepper, coral, and garments. (Information in part from CUDL.)
Seems like an endowment list for the court (maḥkama). Contains an ʿalāma at the top: al-ḥamdu li-llāh rabb al-ʿālamīn. Needs examination.
Legal query concerning a case of levirate marriage; verso: blank; published, with translation, by Friedman, Polygyny, pp. 144–45.

Letter in Arabic script. Portions of four lines are preserved on recto mentioning somebody's son. Verso contains the address: yaṣil hādhā l-kitāb ilā [...]. It should be possible to decipher more of the address.

Draft, in the hand of the scribe Hillel b. Eli (fl. 1066–1108 CE), of an addition to the last will of the parnas Eli ha-Kohen b. Yahya (documents signed by him 1057-1107). In his previous will, drawn up by the Andalusian judge Yiṣḥaq b. Shemuel (see Mediterranean Society, II, p. 512 section 13) Eli had mentioned that one of his partners, Abu al-Muna Tiqwa b. 'Amram from Ascalon (see Mediterranean Society, V, pp. 212-214, 566, 567), owed him forty-eight dinars. The next day the witnesses reported that the partner had testified that Eli had withdrawn about six dinars, whereupon Eli asked them to

Fragment from the top of a state document in Arabic script. There is a basmala, possibly a remnant of a tarjama at upper left, and two lines from the beginning. The second line contains the standard blessings for the caliph (amīr al-muʾminīn) and his ancestors and descendants. Reused on recto for piyyuṭ.

One side: four ethical (?) principles in Judaeo-Arabic written over the remains of a few lines in Arabic. The other side: a legal query and its answer (both in the same handwriting) regarding illicit sexual relationships. ASE.

Most of the fragment consists of accounts in rudimentary Judaeo-Arabic. The word ṭibbī appears in several places, but the names of the commodities are tricky to decipher. As are the names of the customers: Ab[ū] Fadl (with a dāl); Abū Riḍā al-ʿAṭṭ[ā]r; Abū Saʿd (with a shin). There is a list in Arabic script as well, headed Ṣāḥib al-Dukkān: 1/2 raṭl of [...]; 3 ounces of zayt ṭayyib (?); 3 ounces of soap (ṣābūn); 1 raṭl and 3 ounces of verdigris (zinjār); and 3 ounces of qaṭāra [=qaṭrān?]. ASE.

Verso: Fragment from the left side of an early Fatimid decree or other state document. The ends of three lines remain, including the word al-taqsīṭ. Reused on recto by Efrayim b. Shemarya to copy parts of Saʿadya Gaʾon's tafsīr (translation and commentary) on Genesis 1:3 - 1:15
Legal document. In Hebrew and Aramaic. Dating: No later than 1034 CE ([4]7[.]4 AM). It is also possible that the 'ארבע' is 'ארבעין', in which case this would date from 979–89 CE.

Letter to the judge Natan (b. Shelomo?) ha-Kohen (he-ḥaver ha-meʿulle ha-dayyan ha-maskil bet din hagun...). In Judaeo-Arabic. Dating: ca. 12th century. Goitein's index card suggests that the sender could be the addressee's cousin Ṭoviyya b. ʿEli—but the handwriting is not Ṭoviyya's. The purpose of the letter is to ask for help on behalf of the bearer, formerly the tax farmer (ḍāmin) of 'the freight (nawl) of [...]' in Shubrā Damsīs. This man left the city years ago, and he was targeted by his creditors when he returned. The case seems tangled and involves Salāma Ibn al-Muʿallim, 33 dirhams, B

Top part of a legal document in Hebrew. Very faded/damaged. Dated: Tuesday, 27 Nisan of an unknown year; likely 11th century. Bill of release (וכתבתי . . . שטר פיצוי זה . . .). Someone acknowledges receipt of a sum. May mention Yosef in l. 6. Otherwise unclear if any further details are preserved.
Introductory formula of a responsum, directed at Abraham Maimonides. (Information from CUDL)

Letter in Arabic script. Reporting on a dialogue between the sender and someone else about someone who hasn't received a payment, and how the sender hasn't yet left Fustat. Mentions: "... his arrival... every day in a gathering of the Jews on the small fast day (yawm ṣawm al-ṣaghīr)." Mentions the government (al-sulṭān) several times. Mentions "aṣḥābnā al-ḥāḍirīn" (our friends/colleagues who are present). Might mention "the palace" (al-qaṣr, v4), and coming down from it, then "no one should blame me...." Needs further examination.

Letter in Judaeo-Arabic. Yemeni hand? Very damaged and faded. Dating: 12th century. Some of the names mentioned are related to India Book II, such as Yaʿaqov al-ʿAdanī and Maḍmūn. In fact it may be addressed to Maḍmūn ("...yā Maḍmūn lā talūmūnā ʿalā..."). Also mentions the names Sulaymān and Manṣūr. At least part of the letter concerns a shipment of silk. AA. ASE.
Small receipt of some sort for Hilāl al-[...], it seems for 25 + 1/2 + 1/8 nuqra dirhams. Torn down the middle.
Instructions for a magical spell in Judaeo-Arabic.
Legal document, faded, very few words preserved. Mentions shares "ḥiṣṣa".
A formula of a letter to a notable
Letter from Avraham Maghribī to the elder Maʿānī. Mainly in Judaeo-Arabic. This is a recommendation for charity on behalf of the bearer, the son of Yaʿaqov al-Aʿmā (the blind).

Upper part of recto: Legal query probably in the hand of Yedutun ha-Levi, addressed to Moshe Maimonides, ca. 1168–1204 CE (based on the dates when he was active in Egypt). Concerning a cantor who quarreled with a congregant and made an oath never to pray behind him. Now he repents of the oath and wishes to know if he can return to praying with the congregation.
Unidentified text in Arabic, probably a letter. Recto: piyyuṭ. (Information from CUDL)

Possibly accounts for rent from the qodesh. Mentions names such as Abū l-Majd al-Parnas, the brother-in-law of Mūsā al-Ṭawwāf, al-Zaftāwī, Mufaḍḍal b. Sumaysima, Ibn Bū ʿImrān al-Sharābī, Bū ʿImrān b. al-Dajjānī (?), and Moshe al-Baghdādī. And "the order of Sayyidnā."
Late letter, apparently written by a certain Dhārā (?). The marginal section mentions "trousers for children" and something carried or delivered by a certain Meʾīr. (Information partly from CUDL)
Biblical commentary, late. The description of a ketubba under this shelfmark in FGP is probably intended for CUL Or.1080 9.19.
Palimpsest, Pirqey de Rabbi Eliezer in Hebrew over Greek base text (information from FGP).
Small fragment from the top of an official-looking document, headed by basmala and ṣalwala, then al-mamlūk [...]. Potentially a petition.

Account including list of goods and their costs in dirhams, arranged in two columns. Mentions bowls and dishes; sal ammoniac; robes. Verso is headed "beginning of Ramaḍān i.e. Shevaṭ." Mentions: aṣḥāb Dār al-Qarāʾin(?); flax. Expenses are organized according to the day of the week. The account continues with Shawwāl/Adar below. Mentions ṭaḥīn and flour. (Information in part from Baker & Polliack catalogue).
Fragment of an unidentified Arabic document. Reused for Hebrew alphabet practice.

tags: ib-addenda, Alexandria, India Book unedited, IB5
desc: Small fragment from a letter in Judaeo-Arabic. May be in the hand of Abū l-Rabiʿ Sulaymān the son of Abū Zikrī Kohen (cf. ENA NS 33.16 (PGPID 11478) and shelfmarks cited there). Mentions Ibn Elishaʿ, Alexandria, and the number 70 (in the margin).
Verso: Small fragment of a gigantic Fatimid decree.
F. 1r: Arabic document, mentioning "al-bāqī... al-Yahūdī... min al-[...]"; the rest is unidentified. (Information in part from CUDL.)
Verso: extensive accounts in Arabic script and Greek/Coptic numerals. Many names and transactions in raṭls are mentioned. Needs examinationl
Bifolio containing a religious text (or poetry?) in Arabic script, the draft of a letter or petition, Greek/Coptic numerals, and reused for Hebrew  poems/piyyutim with Judaeo-Arabic headings.
Fragment of a letter of appeal for assistance. In the hand of Ḥalfon b. Menashshe ha-Levi (1100–38).

Betrothal contract for Sitt al-Khibāʾ bt. Ṭahor the beadle and Meʾir the cantor, in Fusṭāṭ. The contract stipulates that the bride will lose her delayed marriage gift if she refuses to live together with the husband's daughter (who is possibly an adult already). Marriage payments: 5 + 25 = 30. The heavily decorated late 12th-century ketubba T-S 24.17 may be the marriage contract for this couple. (Information from CUDL.)
Legal document mentioning a ketubba. (Information from CUDL)

State document, internal communication, fragment of a few lines. Mentions a dīwān. Reused for a rabbinic text in Hebrew and Judaeo-Arabic mentioning qumāsh (rubbish/goods/cloth).

NB: This description must belong with a different shelfmark as no text is visible in Arabic script.

Small fragment of a letter in Hebrew. Wide space between the lines. "I arrived safely in Sambūṭya (=Sunbāṭ)... may His blessing fall on him and his son for good, and with heaven's aid, I plan to travel to Damietta and from there to Tinnīs.... his seat... not as warning but only as reminding...." Interestingly, both Damietta and Tinnīs have glosses written above them (אי כפתור and אי חנס respectively).
Mercantile accounts in Judaeo-Arabic. Dating: 11th or 12th century. The hand is that of ʿArūs b. Yosef. Mentions tartar; Yaḥyā; Yosef; a purse
Letter fragment in Judaeo-Arabic, in a very small script, mentioning the family of Abū Sahl and Abū ʿ[...]. (Information from CUDL)
Legal document. In the hand of Ḥalfon b. Menashshe (fl. 1100-1138 CE). Mentions the government and likely two partners and their previous contract. (Information in part from CUDL)

tags: Illness: women's, epidemic: marad, epidemic, illness letter 969-1517, Appeal, Illness
desc: Letter of appeal addressed to a Jewish dignitary (ha-dayyan ha-maskil). The introduction is in Hebrew and the body is in Judaeo-Arabic. The writer prays that the addressee will be spared "the diseases of this year." He states that he is impoverished and suffering from an illness. "If I live, you will see my gratitude for you in public." He asks the addressee to send a messenger to the Nagid on his behalf. The letter contains the interesting oath "wa-ḥaqq al-yiḥud," where yiḥud = tawḥīd. He also writes that al-ḥūrma (his wife?) is as sick as can be. Information in part from Baker/Polliack catal

Bottom of a very faded letter in Judaeo-Arabic, with some Hebrew. Probably a mercantile letter of the 11th century. Mentions Abū l-Faraj, maybe a qāḍī, al-dār al-ḥarīrī(?), and greetings to Moshe Ibn al-Majjānī. Reused on verso for piyyuṭ.

Legal document. Involving appointing an agent; Abū l-[...]; Sitt al-Kull bt. [...]; and demanding maintenance (mezonot). There are a few words in Judaeo-Arabic on verso, including "danānīr." (Information in part from CUDL)
Small fragment from the middle part of a legal document mentioning Avraham Halevi. AA

Recto: Notes for drawing up a legal document. In Judaeo-Arabic. Concerns a woman, half of a house, what will happen when she sells her shares, "renting from the dīwān," and so on. Verso: A similar digest of a legal document in Judaeo-Arabic. Different hand (hand of Ḥalfon b. Menashshe?). Involving a house, various sums of money, and renovating a bustān. This was written on top of a reused fiscal account in Arabic script.

Recto: copy of a letter from Sharira Gaon to Fustat, around 970. The writer asks to renew the community’s support for the Yeshiva. The letter was written soon after Sharira became the Gaon. Verso: an answer for a question about the rules when traveling in a ship during Passover and Shabbat. (Information from Gil, Kingdom. Vol. 2, #24) VMR
Accounts, probably. In Judaeo-Arabic. Damaged and faded. Familiar from other fragments 11th century? Densely written.

Student notebook fragment, 4 folios. 18th- or 19th-century based on the paleography. There are at least three different scribal hands portrayed in the notebook which contains a variety of writing exercises in Hebrew and Judaeo-Arabic. MCD.

Marriage contract (ketubba). Not completed (perhaps because of an error in lines 4 and 5). Location: Fustat. Dated: Elul 1552 Seleucid, which is 1241 CE. Groom: Yeshuʿa ha-Talmid b. Shemuel ha-Levi. Bride: Sitt al-Rashīda bt. Yeshuʿa ha-Talmid, an orphan and a virgin. The document also states that he 'betrothed' her, indicating that there was no formal betrothal which preceded this document. Marriage payments: 40 + 10 = 50. The script resembles that of ʿImmanuel b. Yeḥiel but is not identical. On verso there are jottings in Judaeo-Arabic and Arabic script. (Information from Goitein’s index car

Informal notes in Judaeo-Arabic. Recto: Possibly from Shelomo b. Eliyyahu. The writer asks the addressee to write a note to R. Ḥananel regarding the writer's plan to come into Fustat today to see him as well as the writer's wife. He writes, "By the Covenant, I do not want to go to Gehennom, for most slaughterers are in Gehennom, as they (the rabbis) also said, 'The best of slaughterers go down to Gehennom.'" (This is a slight misquotation of BT Kiddushin 82a, exchanging the negative maxims about physicians and slaughterers). Goitein suggests that the writer is seeking a recommendation to be ap

Recto: Legal document. Dated: beginning of Ṭevet 1457 Seleucid = December 1145 CE. In which Yaḥyā b. Ṣedaqa confirms that a house which he had given to his sister Umm al-[...] (who it seems had meanwhile died) and which was occupied by her son Abū ʿAlī, is given to the latter and his children. 

Verso: Unrelated legal document, specifying conditions for a partnership. (Information from Goitein's index card.)

Fragment of a legal document, mentioning the elder Abū Isḥāq probably relating to a marriage agreement. The monogamy clause is included. The bride was probably Qaraite, based on the phrase ואנה לא יחללהא[ת ...] ט. Refers to her poverty as well. (AA)
Accounts or a letter in Judaeo-Arabic. Mentions thawbs and sending things. Small fragment.
Monograph; from Saadia's formulary of legal documents. (info from FGP)
Numbered list of talmudic tractates and a list of quotations from the Mishna. (Information from CUDL)

Family letter in Arabic script. Numerous greetings to various people are preserved (e.g., to "ahl bayt mawlānā" and the sender's paternal uncle Makārim), also a mention of 'the bearer of this letter.' Needs further examination for content.

Letter in Hebrew and Judaeo-Arabic. There are many elaborate titles on recto (הנכבד החכם והנב[ון] . . . אלעזיזה . . . [אלתל]מיד אלחכם הירא אלהים . . . ). On verso mentions "the people of knowledge' (ahl al-ʿilm) and mentions a certain Yaʿaqov. (Information in part from CUDL)

Fragment from a therapeutical work, dealing here with the treatment of the sort of convulsion known as Umm al-Ṣibyān, dysuria and alopecia. Rue cooked in oil is recommended for dysuria, and when topically applied, it is used to treat alopecia. (Information in part from CUDL.)
Possibly an account, and some jottings including names - needs examination.

Recto: Accounts describing shares given to Avraham b. Farrāḥ and Ḥayyim b. ʿAmmār as deposits. 

Verso: in a different hand (that of Nahray b. Nissim?) mentions prices, quantities (of goods?) and the name Abū Yūsuf. Dating: 11th century. (Information in part from CUDL.)

Legal fragment. Probably a partnership agreement in the hand of Hillel b. ʿEli. Refers to a period of two years and various mutually agreed upon conditions. One of the parties is named Yehuda. Quite faded.
Recto: Beginning of a letter or sermon in Judaeo-Arabic. Addressed to a group of people: "yā aṣḥābnā!" Exhorting them that (false?) accusations are bad and that God has forbidden lashon ha-raʿ.

Note on parchment concerning a purchase. The main text talks about 25 nuqra coins being given to Najīb for the order of a proper Byzantine chest, with lock and key, measuring at the most 60 × 70 × 75. There is also mention of borrowing money for it from Ibn Ṣafī al-Dawla. At the side the words such as bed cover, table, and cutting of copper are listed;  Verso: atbash alphabet. (Information mainly from CUDL.)
Legal fragment.

Recto: Piyyuṭ in the hand of Moshe b. Levi ha-Levi. 

Verso: Two magical spells also in his hand. The purpose of the first one is written at the top but is quite faded and difficult to read. "To be written on a bay leaf and drunk with wine." It is a formulary, as the name has been left ר פ בר פל. The second is "for going out at night" (ללכרוג פי אליל אמסך בדראעך אלבאב וקול ג מראת באל אני מכיר באל אני מכיר אפספס אמן . . סלה).
State document in Arabic. Fragments of 4 lines are preserved.
Recto: lists of prices. Verso: list mentioning Sitt Ghanāʾīm and the leader Abū Manṣūr. (Information from CUDL)
Accounts. Mentions names such as ʿAbdallāh the miller (al-ṭaḥḥān).

Fragment of a letter. 6 lines in Hebrew with praises for an important person (including that God make his enemies drink poison), then 1 line in Judaeo-Arabic beginning a letter of recommendation for the bearer: . . . סבב אצדאר הדה אלכדמה אלי מולאי אלשיך החכם] והנבון הירא שמים יהי אלהיו עז[רו] ואויביו ישקה כוס רעל ויכלה בטוב ימיו ובנעימים שנותיו יחיה לו חמודו . . . השר הנכבד התלמיד המיבין יזכהו לראות בניו ובני בניו ממלאים מקום אבותם הטהורים הקדושים וכן יהי רצון אעלאמה דאם עזה באן חאמלה[א] . . . .
Probably part of a letter. The name Ṣedaqa is mentioned. (Information from CUDL)
An ethical treatise, in a personal tone (yā akhī...), about fulfilling the religious duties

Letter fragment, partly written in Arabic and mostly in written in a Hebrew-script (Judaeo-Arabic) cipher composed of the letters alef through ṭet. A single dot over the letter means to multiply it by 10 (so א̇ becomes י and ב̇ becomes כ, and so on) and a double dot means to multiply it by 100 (so א̇ becomes ק and ב̇ becomes ר, and so on). 

The fragment is quite damaged and the content is difficult to piece together. Mentions the addressee as al-akh al-ajall; a group of people who want money (יטלבון דראהם), "the youth who was writing to you"; the ghulām Sulaymān who went out to the Rīf; the
Literary - recommend suppress
Badly rubbed and faded fragment, probably a document. (Information from CUDL.)
Minute fragment of an Arabic document, possibly. Requires further examination.
Fragment of a letter from the office of Yehoshua Maimonides (b. 1310– d. 1355 CE), possibly a recommendation for Yosef al-Ṣabbān (the soap boiler).

Deed of sale of a part of a house. Location: Alexandria. Dated: last decade of Ḥeshvan 4965 AM = October 1204 CE. Three shares of a house worth 30 dinars (total house worth 240 dinars) are sold for infants and Hebrew and Arabic documents are made out as testimony. Names mentioned: Abū l-Baqāʾ al-Kohen and Abū l-Mufaḍḍal. Signed by the teacher Yehuda b. Aharon the physician (Ibn al-ʿAmmānī). and Yefet b. Moshe. Validated by Anatoli b. Yosef, Eliyya b. Zekharya and Shelomo b. Ḥalfon. (Information from CUDL and Goitein's index card.)

Marriage contract (ketubba). Location: Qujandīm (קגנדים), Egypt. Dated: Thursday, 16 Av 4705 AM = 29 July 945 CE. The document records a marriage gift of only four dinars and is signed by eleven or twelve individuals, including the groom. (Friedman, Jewish Marriage, vol 2, 165–75.) EMS
Fragment of a poetic letter in Hebrew. The beginnings of 21 lines are preserved. Good candidate for a join.
Letter from Eliyyahu the Judge to David ha-Kohen he-Ḥaver. Only the top is preserved. (Information in part from CUDL)
Small, darkened piece of parchment, with phrases both from a letter (top) and from a legal document (bottom).

Verso: Memorial(?) list. Dating: likely 13th century. Contains also a few names of women. Every entry is preceded by "bayt"/"house of." The names: Isḥāq al-Ṭabbākh; Makīn b. Mardūkh; Abū l-Riḍā al-Ḥakīm; Abū ʿAlī al-Manāshifī; the female teacher (al-muʿalllima); Fāḍila; Masʿūd; Manṣūr; Mordekhay; Abū l-Faḍl; Mufaḍḍal; Abū l-Munā; Menaḥem; his sister; Abū l-Faraj al-Kohen; Ibrāhīm b. Sulaymān; Rashīd b. al-Ḥakīm; Umm ʿAzīz; Ibrāhīm al-Khayyāṭ; Nāṣīr b. al-ʿAfīf; Abū ʿAlī; Munajjā al-Ṣabbāgh; Yosef al-Kohen; al-Khayyāṭa; al-Jazzār; Umm Budayr.
Accounts of Abū l-Khayr, mentioning ships and quantities of different wares. Mentions Nahray and Ibn Lanjū. (Information in part from CUDL)
Accounts, probably for wine sent to the castle (burj), with sums of money in silver of good quality and mentioning the names of Yaʿaqov Ṭayyib and Moše Ṭayyib.
Letter from Mordekhay Ashkenazi to a family member. In Hebrew. Dating: Late. Needs examination.

Letter written by a man on behalf of his wife to her brother, inviting him to come out to the countryside for a full month to find relief from his stress and also to bring his boys with him, who would be better off in the countryside than in bible school. (Information from Mediterranean Society, V, p. 532)

tags: Ibn al-Ba'ba', tax receipt, ships, qarib, Shipwreck, khums, fayj
desc: Letter from Mūsā b. Abī l-Ḥayy, Alexandria, to Nahray b. Nissim. Offers details of ill-fated ships that were destroyed in a storm or met with the Byzantine navy. Of the ships that had been in al-Kanāʾis (a port in western Egypt), the only ones that had made it all the way to Alexandria were 7 ships of al-Ishfīlī, and one qārib apiece of Ibn Dayṣūr, Ibn Sindūr, Ibn al-Dajdāj, Ibn al-Jannānī and al-Jazūla — 12 in all. An unnamed enemy stopped one ship, and the others fled; and only 5 ships managed to set out on their way. Gil connects this with the 15 ships mentioned in T-S 8J27.2, his #447, and
Address (אלשיך אלאגל) and jottings. (Information from CUDL)
Letter by Yosef b. Musa Tāhartī from Alexandria containing details about shipments of flax including. List of expenditures. (Information from M. Gil, Kingdom, Vol. III, p. 260)
List of names and numbers- money collected and owed. Probably written by Shelomo b. Elya

Legal document. Bill of divorce in the hand of Shelomo b. Eliyyahu ha-Dayyan, Fusṭāṭ. Dated: 5 Sivan 1524 (26 May 1213). This bill of divorce is one of forty under the T-S 10J2 shelfmark. The fragment is rather irregularly shaped, and the lack of signatures indicates that the divorce was not finalized; it was later completed two months later in NLI 577.4/27. The divorce was to be between Mufaḍḍal b. Mesullam and Nasab bt. Manṣūr, whose father is referred to in this document by his Arabic name, and in the completed bill by his Hebrew name Elʿazar. Shelomo b. Eliyyahu's handwriting in this docum

Letter from Yosef b. Musa al-Tāhartī, probably from Mahdiyya, to Ya’aqov b. Nahum, Fustat. Around 1045. Regarding a very large amount of goods and deals. Mentions mainly types of silk, different fabrics, and peals. Several things in this letter are mentioned in the letter from Yeshua b. Isma’Il al-Tāhartī (see T-S 12.389). (Information from Gil, Kingdom, Vol. 3, #359) VMR

Letter of business in which the writer requests the recipient purchase for him a measure of oil, two ‘futa’ (sari-like cloth), and two dinars of dried fruit (‘zabib’). Abu Imran, Abu al-Rida, and the town of Qus are mentioned, and the writer sends greeting to Abu al-Faraj and Yishaq. EMS (Information from Goitein's index cards)

The sender has spoken to Ibn al-ʿIrāqī, who reports that he sent all the letters to their addressees "after the conquest of the land" (futūḥ al-balad); he asks the addressee to try to sell the indigo and buying with its price khazāsh (low-quality silk) or fūṭas (wrap

Bifolio containing lists of Hebrew terms. 

On the righthand page of verso, there are jotted accounts in Arabic and Greek/Coptic numerals.

Letter from Gaʾon Shelomo b. Yehuda, probably in Jerusalem or Ramla, to Efrayim b. Shemarya, in Fustat. Dating: 13 Kislev [4803 AM] = 29 November 1042 CE, based on Gil's assessment and, in broad strokes, ca. 1025–1051 CE based on the years when Shelomo b. Yehuda served as Gaʾon. In Hebrew, with the address in Arabic. Written shortly after the resolution of the political conflict with Natan b. Avraham, who by this time had been demoted to Av Bet Din. Shelomo b. Yehuda is worried about a tax in Egypt as he heard that a census had been taken of the poor with the idea of imposing the tax also on t
Minute fragment from a Judaeo-Arabic letter. (Information from CUDL)

Court notebook (continuation of T-S 8K 20.1.1). Record #3 (fol. 2r): Maḥfūẓ b. Yiṣḥaq al-ʿAzāzī (i.e., from ʿAzāz, north of Aleppo) sues Yosef b. Avraham for a sum of money. They are each questioned, Yosef denies that he owes that much, and Maḥfūẓ says that he will come back with witnesses. They make an appointment for 30 Nisan (~1 month later). No signatures. #4 (fol. 2v): Yeshuʿa b. Ṣadaqa sues Yosef b. Seʿadya for a dinar. "Long story short: they compromised at 1/2 dinar." 1/4 is to be paid now and 1/4 at the time of 'travel' (i.e., when they are next together). #5 (also on fol. 2v): Mubāra

Upper half of a Hebrew letter addressed to the majlis of (the Nagid) Abū Zikrī (Yehuda) b. Saʿadya. Address in Judaeo-Arabic on verso. Written in an elevated register. Likely a request for assistance of some kind. There are good chances of finding a join.
Arabic poetry.

Betrothal record from 1093 in which the obligatory betrothal gift is 4 and one/sixth dinars. The document also stipulates the daughter receives the uppermost floor of a house; if she preferred to live elsewhere, she would receive rent, but her father and his heirs were responsible for the payment of the ground rent and watchman. Signed by Eli ha-Kohen b. Yahya, Avraham b. Yiṣḥaq (the Scholar), and Ezekiel II ha-Kohen he-Ḥaver b. Eli he-Ḥaver I. (S. D. Goitein, Mediterranean Society, 2:522, 3:445, 4:96, 374) EMS

tags: Moshe b. Levi, booklist, to edit
desc: Book list in the hand of Moshe b. Levi ha-Levi. See T-S K3.41 for a similar booklist in his hand (possibly but not clearly a join).
Legal testimony. Upper right corner. Mentions Maṣliaḥ Gaon. A man makes a declaration beginning with "Eight _____ ago...."
Letter, late, in Judaeo-Arabic from Avraham [...] to Hayyim [...]. Needs further examination.

tags: Yefet b. Menashshe, Halfon b. Menashshe, illness: eye
desc: Fragment from a business letter probably written by Yefet b. Menashshe to his brother Halfon (the address is not visible). Abu al-Fadl is mentioned and ruba'i of 'anzrut (= Sarcocolla, mentioned in medical books in recipes for the treatment of eye complaints such as redness, itching , and eye diseases).

Accounts in Judaeo-Arabic and Hebrew. Sephardi hand. Dating: The date appears once on recto and again on verso. Possibly Wednesday, 6 Kislev 5455 AM (התנ׳׳ה), but the reading of the tens place digit is tentative. Mentions names such as Sulaymān, Raḥamim, Yona, Yaʿaqov, and a gabbay named Reuven.

Literary treatise in Judaeo-Arabic on the laws of mourning in various special cases. when the deceased is the father of a bride; if he was executed by the court; if he committed suicide; if he rejected rabbinic authority (al-madhhab al-rabbānīyya, sunanuhum) (in this case there is no mourning, but rather celebration); if he has no one to mourn for him; and how there is no mourning on shabbat (verso). Also on verso are several lines in Judaeo-Arabic giving formulaic opening phrases for a letter. ASE.

Legal document mentioning a certain Ibn Mihnab (?) ("son of the idiot"). In the hand of Ḥalfon b. Menashshe (fl. 1100-1138 CE). Refers to moving from a man's house to somewhere else. Also to 'the rent of the middle.' (Information in part from CUDL)
Another copy of the same letter as in Bodl. MS heb. b 3/19 + Bodl. MS heb. b 3/20; see PGPID 5595 for details. (Information from Goitein's index card.)
Recto: Fragment of a letter from [...] Fasi the cantor b. Shelomo, the cantor, to Efrayim b. Shemarya (fl. 1007–1055 CE).
Both pages are covered with jottings and scribal practice in Hebrew and Arabic. There may also be the remnants of a legal document in Judaeo-Arabic.
Tax receipt. Needs examination.

Bifolio of accounts in Arabic and Greek/Coptic numerals. Very neat chancery-esque handwriting and striking arrangement on the page. Possibly of a landlord? The entries have headers such as makhzan; al-dār al-maʿrūfa bi-Ibn Dāwūd; duwayra; duwayra; makhzan; duwayra; ḥānūt; ḥānūt. Merits further examination.

Letter in Judaeo-Arabic. Dating: likely ca. 13th or 14th century. Very distinctive handwriting with crescent-shaped nun sofits. The sender seems disgruntled that someone didn't accept his help setting up a shop; he also owes two months of rent. Greetings to various people including the addressee’s father. (Information in part from CUDL)

Accounts in Arabic script and Greek/Coptic numerals. Mentions people such as Ibrāhīm al-Ṣayrafī and the brother-in-law of Abū l-Manṣūr. Mentions the jāliya, blanket/cloak (malḥafa), natron, bread, and various other items.

Legal document(s) or letter(s) concerning a legal case. Both sides—one in Arabic script, one in Judaeo-Arabic—are first-person declarations about the details of some financial case involving al-Shaykh al-ʿAfīf. The Arabic side includes the phrase "annanī mā aʿūd uṭālibuhu" (I will not sue him any more).
Note/receipt/account of some kind: "Abū Manṣūr collected 16 dirhams and I collected 20 dirhams," apparently the price of wheat (al-qamḥ al-mabīʿ?).

Trousseau list. In Judaeo-Arabic. Fragment (bottom part only). Rudimentary hand. Entries include Dustarī/Tustarī fabric, other garments, and a female slave valued at 30 dinars. The early and delayed marriage payments (muqaddam wa-muʾakhkhar) amount to 150 dinars. Dowry items listed are worth 188 dinars (but note that all jewelry items are missing and only the end of the clothing list is preserved). RR

Legal document. A very thorough release that involves Abū Zikrī al-Kohen. Unclear if any more details of the case are preserved. (NB: There may be Goitein notes somewhere, but they are currently missing.)
Receipt in Arabic and Hebrew script for a purse full of coins from Nahray b. Nissim to Mūsā b. Abī l-Ḥayy in Alexandria.
Accounts for construction or building maintenance in Judaeo-Arabic and Greek/Coptic numerals.
A page from Ḥanane'l b. Shemuʾel, Sefer ha-Miṣvot. An autograph. For joins see the long list in FGP. (AA)
Halakhic discussion regarding the slaughter of animals.

Receipt for the capitation tax of Ibrāhīm b. Yūsuf the Jew, a silk worker (qazzāz) and craftsman (ṣāniʿ). Same payer: T-S Ar.34.224, T-S Ar.34.282 (where he is called qazzāz wa-ʿaṭṭār instead), T-S Ar.35.55, and T-S Ar.35.22.

Fragment of a letter in Judaeo-Arabic. Very faded. Dating: likely 13th century. 

Verso: פי הדא אלאסבוע . . . . חתי יגי אכוה . . . ימצי . . . חנא אלא מא גדד עלינא מן אלחזן . . . אלבכא רגאל ונסא . . . חתי אלסרואל . . . [ס]מעתה לא . . . .

Recto:
. . . מן . . . מציב[ה] . . . אן ו . . . . . . . . . . . . .ובקי פי אלאכיר מע אלחרב(?) . . . . . פי אלאכיר כלצ . . . . . 

Possibly an indirect join with T-S K25.279 (PGPID 35289). ASE
Literary - recommend suppress”

Astrological text in Judaeo-Arabic with an interesting geographical section, describing the different locations under the influence of Leo, including "the lands of the Turks" and the cities that were founded under similar constellations, including Iṣfahān, Raʾs al-ʿAyn, al-Ruhā (Edessa), Latakia, Fustat, Ṣadā(?), and Dīnāwar אלדינואר (= Dīnavar دينور?). 

The latter site Dīnavar was a prominent city during Late Antiquity and the early medieval centuries but may have been abandoned as early as the fourteenth century. Its Encyclopaedia Iranica entry lists the city's location as 34° 35’ N, 47°

Letter from Ṭoviyya b. ʿEli ha-Kohen to his cousin the judge Natan b. Shelomo of Fustat. In Judaeo-Arabic. Ṭoviyya says that he is sending some wheat and asks for instructions about the price for which the rest should be sold. Dating: ca. 1140 CE. (Information from Mediterranean Society, I, p. 425; V, p. 516, and from Goitein's index cards)
Business letter in Persian.

Late list of names. Dating: 18th or 19th century based on the paleography. Many names are mentioned: Zaki Sansino (Soncino), David Avigdor, Yosef Arukh, David Barselona(?), Lieto Mizrahi, Bekhor Sanbari, Elyaqim Dayyan.
Small fragment of a letter in Arabic. Faded. Mentions 'al-shaykh adāma ʿizzahū' and 'mawlāy'

Recto: Marriage document (ketubba) in Palestinian style. Dated: [47]40 AM = 979/80 CE. Groom: Efrayim b. [...]. Bride: Khuzayr bt. Ḥusayn. (Information from Friedman, Jewish Marriage, vol. 2, 226–36) Verso: The end of a halakhic treatise on clean and unclean animals, meat preparation etc. (Infromation from CUDL)

Receipt for the capitation tax of Mūsā b. Futūḥ al-Yahūdī. Location: Alexandria. Amount: 2 dinars. Same cluster:

T-S AS 180.22 (PGPID 37373)

T-S NS 327.43 (PGPID 25835)

Fragment of a letter sent from Alexandria to the Head of the Congregations, perhaps R. Eliyyahu the Dayyan, describing a meeting of about fifty elders headed by R. Shemuel, the Dayyan and Ras al-Jaliya (the Nasi). Regret is expressed about a letter sent by the Nagid Avraham, and about letters by the addressee (Information from Goitein's index cards) Letter to someone addressed as ‘Adon ha-Tora Sar he-Te'uda Rosh ha-Qahal Yehid ha-Dor', concerned with community matters, sent to the perfumer's market to Abu l-Faraj (?). Mentions people and titles including the Nagid Abraham, Sulayman, Shemuʾel a

Letter from Natan ha-Kohen b. Yosef to Yiṣḥaq ha-Kohen b. Yaʿaqov the judge, whom he calls his son. He writes about some small business matters and asks about his sick wife (wajaʿ al-bayt, r8–9). (Information from Goitein, Mediterranean Society, III, p. 160, and Goitein's index cards.) Alternate description: Letter to ‘my son’ Isaac ha-Kohen b. Jacob the judge from ‘his father’ Nathan ha-Kohen b. Joseph (obviously not father and son in the strict biological sense, as he also sends greetings to Jacob the judge, the actual father), concerned with business matters, for example the trade of indigo
Legal document, (iqrār), in Arabic script. Ḥusayn b. Yaḥyā testifies. Refers to the year 501 H which would be 1107/08 CE. Needs examination.

Legal document. In Judaeo-Arabic. In the hand of Ḥalfon b. Menashshe. Concerning [...] b. Hillel ha-Zaqen, Yosef b. Moshe ha-Kohen (see T-S NS 321.12 (PGPID 9213)), [...] al-Maḥallī, possibly Ibn Asad, and partnership dealings. Mentions 20 dinars.
Minute fragment from a legal deed written by Halfon b. Menashshe Halevi (1100-1138 CE).
Secondary use: Hebrew piyyuṭ and jottings in at least two different hands. One of the Hebrew lines refers to Yehuda ha-Nagid ve-Rosh (i.e., Yehuda b. Saʿadya).

Letter in Judaeo-Arabic. Fragment (right side of recto). Mentions "the people of Fustat/Egypt... the day I departed... my livelihood...." On verso, the continuation of the letter and a few words and jottings in Arabic script (probably remnants from an earlier document). (Information from CUDL)

Deed of sale. Location: Fustat. Dated: Thursday, end of Tammuz 4764 AM = 1315 Seleucid = July 1004 CE. In which Khalaf b. Yosef b. Yaʿaqov sells his 8 shares of a house (one third of the total 24 shares), which borders the house of Ben Masīḥ the Christian, to Yeḥezqel b. Masʿūd al-ʿAqrabānī, for the sum of 70 Muʿizzī dinars. Witnessed by Shemuel b. Ḥanokh, Shelomo b. Yosef ha-Kohen, Shelomo b. Ṣedaqa, Saʿadya b. Avraham, Asad b. Ṣedaqa ha-Kohen, Shelomo b. Avraham b. ʿUlla, Aharon b. David al-Raqqī, Hiba b. Aharon, and Yeshuʿa b. ʿEli ha-Kohen. This house appears again in a lawsuit by Yeḥezqel

Recto: testimony within a legal document or a letter, concerning financial matters (power of attorney) and mentioning Abū l-Ba[rakāt?]. Verso: probably small fragment from a legal document in a different hand. (Information in part from CUDL)
Account in Judaeo-Arabic, with some Arabic script and Coptic numerals. Mentions a kerchief; the owner of the veil (miqnaʿa), an old woman and a robe; and flax.

Verso: Remnant of a Fatimid state document, likely a decree. No full words are preserved, but the bottom half of one line and the top half of the next line are visible. Reused for Hebrew literary text.

Deed of sale of an enslaved woman named Shaʿal (or Shuʿl or Shuʿal). Written in the hand of Hillel b. ʿEli. Dated: Last third of Kislev 1420 Seleucid, which is late-November or early-December 1108 CE. Seller: Abū l-Ḥasan Menashshe b. Seʿadya ha-Kohen known as Ibn al-Maṣmūda(?). Buyer: Ṣedaqa b . Yehuda. Price: 21 dinars. Signed by: Yiṣḥaq b. Shemuel ha-Sefaradi, Yosef b. Yaʿaqov, Yeḥezqel b. ʿEli ha-Kohen he-Ḥaver. (Information from Goitein's attached notes.)

Piyyuṭ for Shabbat Balaq with a colophon. "By Ibn al-Shaṭnāsh (אלשטנאש/الشطناش), may God have mercy on him. Written by the cantor Abū l-Ḥasan the son of the cantor Muʿammar, may God have mercy on him, Ibn al-Jāzfīnī." T-S H15.10 has a piyyuṭ by the same poet (Yosef Ibn Abiṭur).
Marriage contract between Eli b. Qimoy and Sutayt b. Yair, written by Shemarya b. Elhanan. Dated Shevat 1306/995 (January-February). (Information from Bareket, Shafrir misrayim, p. 272)

Official-looking corespondence in Arabic script, maybe part of a petition. Mentions a community 'raising' something to a certain Dīwān al-Kh[āṣṣ?]: حاله الى ان يرفع الجماعة الى ديوان الخـ[اص(؟) . . . في مثلها . . .

Letter fragment in Judaeo-Arabic. Mentioning 20 irdabb of wheat that the writer has stored in an apartment in his house, and how he got a fright when he received the addressee's request. (Information in part from CUDL)
Letter addressed to Abū Yaʿqūb [...] b. Nissim. In Judaeo-Arabic. Small fragment. Mentions Yehuda Rosh Kall[a?]. Possibly a request for help or charity.

Drafts of legal documents, one involving a certain Mordekhay b. Manṣūr and a sum of 5 peraḥīm (Venetian gold ducats or a similar coinage type). Dating is 16th- or 17th-century based on the paleography.
Likely an order or receipt. Names al-Shaykh Bū l-Qāsim b. al-[...]
Bill of gift and release granted to grandchildren. In the hand of Halfon b. Menashshe ha-Levi (fl. 1100–1138 CE). One of the parties name is ʿAmram. AA
Fiscal register, in Arabic script.
Unidentified document in Latin script, probably Spanish. Needs examination.

Verso: Document in Arabic script mentioning the words al-waraq (paper) or more likely al-wariq (silver money), 28 dirhams, and a date, which looks like the beginning of Ṣafar 598 AH, which would be 1201 CE if read correctly. Needs further examination. ASE
Ketubba fragment. Small piece. In the hand of Yosef b. Shemuel b. Seʿadya.
Recto: probably a document or letter. Verso: possibly a document, mentioning Moses. (Information from CUDL)
Unidentified document in Arabic script. Extremely faded.
Booklist?

Letter from Moshe Maimonides to a certain Shemuel. Autograph. In Hebrew. Dating: ca. 1168–1204 CE, based on the years when Maimonides was active in Egypt. In this letter, he apologizes for an unspecified lapse and begging indulgence. On verso there is a writing exercise of poetry in Arabic script (including إِذا كُنتَ في نِعمَةٍ فَاِرعَها فَإِنَّ المَعاصي تُزيلُ النِعَم which is known from other sources and attributed to ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib).

Book list, perhaps older than recto: "The goods that belong to Rabbenu Yiṣḥaq.. delivered to Abū(?) Yaʿqūbb." Books include al-Manṣūrī and the poems of al-Ḥarizi. (Information from Goitein's note card) ASE

Verso: Inventory (thabt al-ḥawāʾij). In the hand of Ḥalfon b. Menashshe (fl. 1100–1138 CE). "Date not recorded. Items are listed in two columns. Probably an appendix of an estate of a deceased. There are 5 lines that divide the list into 6 sections. The list comprises items such as: a lamp (manāra) (l. 5) a ring (khātam) (l. 17), precious stones such as corals (ʿaqīq), stones (ḥijr), pearls (luʾluʾ) (ll. 21–22), and many others. This document was not signed." (Information from Gershon Weiss.)
Text headed אדגה דקהלת; several joins are listed on FGP.

Fragment of a bifolio containing a letter or legal declaration in Judaeo-Arabic. It has to do with asserting the rights of a muqaddam (Jewish communal leader) and how the community will not oppose him. Names Ibrāhīm b. ʿUthmān and his son.

Legal document in Arabic script. Dated: 426 AH = 1034/35 CE. The year 424 is also mentioned in the body of the document (l. 1). The document concerns the tax farming rights over a certain district (nāḥiya, ll. 3, 6). Mentions capitation taxes (jawālī) and seed advances (taqāwī) (l. 4). Witnesses include Jāmiʿ b. Abī l-[...]; Musāfir b. Abī l-Ḥusayn; Abū Ṭāhir b. [...]; Ibrāhīm b. ʿĪsā b. Muḥammad al-Khatīb(?). Merits further examination.
Accounts in Judaeo-Arabic, also on remaining space of the recto.

desc:
Verso: Autograph order in the hand of Avraham Maimonides (r. 1205–1237 CE). Mainly in Arabic script with some Hebrew script. Abū l-Majd is to do something for the bearer, a judge (? looks like al-dayyān).

T-S K25.240 consists of small written orders, partly in Hebrew and partly in Arabic script, for monthly payments, made out of the rent-revenue from the pious foundation (waqf) 'Compound of the Poor' or from the pious foundation made by the physician al-Muhadhdhab. All dated orders are from spring and summer, 1218. (Information from Mediterranean Society, II, pp. 420-421, App. A 48-92; pp.

Recto (secondary use): Order issued by David ha-Nasi to Maḥfūẓ and Sālim the parnasim (al-farānisa). They are to disburse (yuṭliq... mimmā taḥta yadihim) a sum of 40 (or 440?) wariq dirhams for the provisioning(?) of the retinue (? ghilmān) of someone titled al-Ajall al-Afḍal.

tags: Illness: khutta, mail-order medicine, fight, Arabic address, illness: recovered, illness letter 969-1517, Illness, illness: pleurisy
desc: Letter from the schoolmaster Natan b. Shemuel, in a small town, to his brother Abū l-Ḥasan, in Fustat. In Judaeo-Arabic, with the address in Arabic script. The writer asks for some ophthalmic medicine, some sour-grape kohl, and an unidentified medicine (רישאנא?), because he needs them very much. If his financial situation were not so terrible this winter, he would have sent some money to cover the cost. He describes his extreme hardships, explaining that he had had to pawn garments to cover the costs of the holidays(?). He asks the addressee to meet with their in-law Abū Naṣr and thank him and
Possibly a fragment from a fiscal register. Mentions a kharājī year. Very large script. Reused for the morning benedictions for weekday services.
Ketubba fragment. See Goitein's index card.
Letter from Shelomo b. Yehuda, probably to Avraham b. Sahlan (died ca. 1032). Dating: approximately 1026 (per Gil) but it is worth noting that Shelomo b. Yehuda signs without Gaonic honorifics.
Accounts in Judaeo-Arabic. Hand of ʿArūs b. Yosef. Dating: 11th or 12th century.

Accounts in Arabic script (3 lines) and Greek/Coptic numerals (dozens of lines). In the Arabic script section, there is a basmala and then perhaps the name al-shaykh Abū Zikrī (adāma Allāh ʿizzahū). The blank spaces have been filled with piyyutim (yoṣerot).

Recto: Petition addressed to Maṣliaḥ Gaʾon (r. 1127–39). In Hebrew and Judaeo-Arabic, beautifully written but with rudimentary spelling. From a woman who had been married for 15 years, complaining about neglect and asking Maṣliaḥ to intervene with her husband to grant her divorce and payment of her dues. (Information from Mediterranean Society, III, p. 186 and from CUDL.)

Small fragment of a state document, likely a decree. Only two lines are preserved, written in very large letters with huge line spacing between them: "... wa-akmal niʿma wa-afḍal umniya..." 

Reused on recto for piyyut.

tags: ib-addenda, Arabic script, India Book unedited, Aden
desc: Letter in Arabic script. The writer is in Aden. He reports that something of the addressee's is safe in his keeping. "If his (or your?) son arrives to Aden this year, I will give him the letter. . . and if he does not arrive to Aden, and I learn his whereabouts, I will write to him." ASE.

IB ח93. Legal query written by Ḥalfon b. Netanʾel, possibly from ʿAydhāb, to an unnamed sage (הדרת יקרת אדונינו הרב הגדול יחיד הדור ופלאו ממזרח שמש עד מבואו אב בית דין שלכל י̇ש ירום הודו והדרו . . . אדונינו נר גלותינו אור עינינו). 
Ḥalfon wrote this as an appendix to an earlier query (which has either not survived or not been identified) "on the shore due to the haste of the messenger" (v13–15). The query concerns complicated cases in the laws of levirate marriage: a woman who heard by rumor that her husband had been killed, who had refused to enter into levirate marriage, and who then died,
Legal document. Bottom part only. Unclear if any of the identifying details are preserved.
Fragment of an Arabic official document reused for Hebrew piyyuṭ on both sides in the hand of a prolific scribe.

Ketubba fragment (upper left corner). Bride: Bahiyya bt. Yosef, a virgin. Early marriage payment: 20 dinars. Dating: ca. 1040 CE (per Goitein). There is a one-line header (superscription), as in (the documents of?) Yefet b. David. (Information from Goitein's index card.)
Fragment of a letter of appeal for charity. In Hebrew, in a calligraphic, square book hand. The petitioner is unable to pay his (or her) debts.

Recto: Fragment of a Judaeo-Arabic letter. Verso: A scrawled record of a property lease dated 23 Nisan 1539 Seleucid = 1228 CE. The renter is Abū Naṣr al-Levi b. Abū l-Maʿānī al-Levi (ZL), and the property owner is Abū Saʿd b. al-Rayyis Mufaḍḍal (ZL).
Accounts. Mentioning many names. Dating: Probably 12th or 13th century. Detailed, clearly written, and large—merits further examination.
Arabic literary work containing remedies.

Letter draft from the Rabbanite leaders of Fustat/Cairo to the Rabbanite leaders of Ashqelon. Dating: Summer 1099 CE. The letter recounts how the Nagid Mevorakh exhorted the Jews of the community to donate money for the redemption of captives and Torah scrolls, and how in response the Jews of Fustat have donated 123 dinars. The first transcription here is for DK 242, and the second is for T-S AS 146.3. For a detailed discussion, see Goldman, "Arabic-Speaking Jews in Crusader Syria" (diss.), 42–48.
Accounts of the bookseller. People mentioned: Bū l-Ḥasan. See also the description for the whole notebook Bodl. MS heb. f 22/19–52 (PGPID 33686).

Business letter in which the sender writes that he is concerned after meeting in Qus a business relation to whom he was able to sell three dinars worth of white linen while the buyer also paid him thirty-two dinars minus one fourth. Reused on verso for copious accounts in Arabic script.

End of a letter in Judaeo-Arabic. Same hand as F 1908.44DD, which is very likely the beginning of the same letter. Dating: No earlier than the 15th century, based on the use of muayyadis (minted by al-Mu'ayyad, beginning in 1415 CE) and ashrafīs.

Karaite purchase deed. Ovadya b. Gedalyah Feyruz is buying a lobby and upper hall from the widow Estīta and her two unnamed daughters from her predeceased husband Aharon Rofe. Dated Monday, Adar 2nd 5446 AM (1686 CE). The scribe Barūkh Rofe and several others signed as witnesses, namely: Shemuʾel Berakha, Moshe Ḥazan, Yeshūʿa Rofe, Raḥamīm [Berakha] (see l. 17), Yosef Miʿmār, Yosef ____(?).

Bill of divorce (get). Location: Al-Saʿdiyya, a part of Ṣanʿāʾ in Yemen, based on the landmarks listed: בירין דמיין נבעין דילה. This locational designation appears in a variety of other documents issued in Ṣanʿā, for example: Sassoon 1055a (PGPID 911), Moss. VII,19 (PGPID 18637). Dated: 29 Tishrei 2023 Seleucid = 12 October 1711 CE. Husband: Yehuda b. Muʿawwiḍa. Wife: Zahra bt. Yaḥyā. Witnesses include: Zekharya b. Yosef. Verso: A separate document is visible through the back of the paper, which may have been pasted to the recto itself or the piece of archival cardboard that is visible around
Newly treated and encapsulated, must be examined
Formulary for a שטר מכירת חזקה. Late, probably belongs with Bodl. MS heb. d 66/100 and is therefore c.1750s.
Accounts in Judaeo-Arabic. In a common hand previously misattributed to ʿArūs. Mentions Abū Manṣūr.
Newly treated and encapsulated, must be examined
Recto: Letter in Judaeo-Arabic between family members. Interesting orthography: אלשעאר for אלצגאר. Mentions "the water in the khalīj (canal)."

Four different documents in the hand of Ḥalfon b. Menashshe (fl. 1100–1138 CE). Clockwise from upper left:

(1) Thin vertical strip from the left side of a document. Involves a certain Aharon and maybe Ḥassūn (l.2). Probably a partnership agreement dividing expenses and profits.

(2) Fragment (upper left piece) of a legal document. Involves: a woman's death; her mother and/or mother-in-law; Sitt al-Ahl; Abū l-Faraj Netanʾel; Ibn Qasāsa (this may be part of the name of Abū l-Faraj Netanʾel); a deceased Abū l-Faḍl. On verso is a list of names, quantities, and goods (such as rose water and fl

List of payments in the name of S[eñor] Yeshuʿa related to ownership or a lease for a house that is dated in across a range of years: Elul [55]97AM // Tevet [55]99 – Tishrei [5]600AM which encompasses 1836-1840CE. In line 11r the fragment clearly switches hands to a less orderly style yet the same form/content of recordkeeping continues. The verso is blank except for staining. MCD.
Unidentified text, in Arabic script. Probably magical due to the humanoid figure at the side. Needs examination.

tags: jaliya, 14th c, Yehoshua Maimonides, tax, capitation tax, jizya
desc: Letter from the office of Yehoshua Maimonides (d. 1355 CE) dealing with the capitation tax and with the kashrut of meat, first half of the 14th c.
State document, in Arabic script. Mentions "خلد الله" towards the end and "رسالة عالي" in the second line. Reused for an order of payment on verso. Needs examination.

tags: cheque, order of payment, India Book, IB5
desc: IB V, 40b. Verso: order of payment by Abū Zikrī Kohen for one half raṭl of soap and the same of perfume. Information from CUDL. Formerly Moss. L 159.3
Prognostications in Judaeo-Arabic. Numbered.

Mercantile letter in Judaeo-Arabic. Fragment (right side of recto). Sent from an unidentified writer, in Damsīs, to his 'brother', probably to Fustat. Dating: 11th century. Mentions Barhūn and a robbery (נזלו עליה לצוץ) (recto l.5); the addressee's mother praying for him (recto l. 10 and verso l. 4); documents including a power of attorney (recto l. 11); Yosef and Nissim al-Muʿallim (recto l. 12); an instruction to find someone to comb (flax) (recto l. 16); news of the ships and the commodities arriving from the West (recto right margin); Abū Yūsuf (recto top margin); and concluding greetings

Drafts or copies of phrases from official correspondence. Medieval-era. The two main sections both seem incomplete and unrelated to each other. The first has to do with a report of somebody's death in Dhū l-Ḥijja 521 AH = January 1127 / February 28 CE ( ولما انهي سقوطه بالوفاة في ذي الحجة سنة احدى وعشرين و[خمسماىة] اعلم بذلك . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .سنة احدى وعشرين وخمسماىة). The second has to do with Jaʿfar and Ṣubḥ(?) the sons of Wafiyy al-Dawla, who are of the Afḍalī continent (min al-ṭāʾifa al-afḍaliyya) and hold a certain iqṭāʿ valued at a certain amount (واما جعفر وصبح(؟) ولدي وفي ال
Bifolio of accounts in Judaeo-Arabic and Hebrew numerals. Mentions someone named Yāsīn al-Shāmī; many other names are listed.
Newly treated and encapsulated, must be examined
Letter in Hebrew with wide space between the lines. Fragment.
Letter fragment. In Ladino. Mentions R. Nissim. Very faded.

Legal query and responsum in Arabic script. The query is written in a tiny handwriting with a thin pen, begins with the words alladhī dhakarahū wa-ashhada bihi aṭāla allāh baqā ḥaḍrat mawlāya al-qāḍī al-ajall. The responsum, written with thick pen, reads among other things qad ḫaraǧa ʾamrunā ʾilayhim bi-miṯl ḏālik wa qad taqaddamnā ʾilayhim ...

Line 2 may include a name, maybe al-Ḥasan b. Ṣāliḥ b. al-Ḥasan al-Dāwudī. Line 5 may refer to "bi-l-yahūd" (in the Jewish courts) or else bi-l-shuhūd ("with the witneses"). It's not clear that the writing with the thick pen has to do with the content

Accounts on a small bifolio, mostly mathematical calculations without any headings or context provided. The verso includes a brief note mentioning the amount of funds requested from a certain Nissīm Benyamīn. The paleography makes is possible to estimate the dating as 16th-century or later. MCD.
Legal document (or 2 documents) in the hand of Ḥalfon b. Menashshe (fl. 1100–1138 CE). The one on the right involves a marriage. The one on the left is signed by Avraham b. Shemaʿya.

Court notebook.

Recto, right side, continuing onto verso, left side: Probably a legal query addressed to the Nagid (al-ḥaḍra al-ṭāhira). Needs examination.

P4: Legal document in the hand of Ḥalfon b. Menashshe (fl. 1100–1138 CE). Deathbed will of Yefet b. Yaʿaqov. He wills that his share in the rent of a house that he held in partnership with others (Ibn al-Dhahabī, Avraham al-Fuqqāʿī, Avraham b. [...], Abū Manṣūr al-Zayyāt) should be spent in two equal shares, one on bread for the poor and the other on a person specified by name. (Information from Goitein, Med Soc II, App. A, no. 180.)
Bottom right corner of a 14th C legal contract, probably a contract, dated 27th Muḥarram 723 AH.

Descriptions of the contents of a collection of books in two different hands: the first, neater block names Yehudah b. Yahya and the text of the Tāj and Bereshit Rabbah and the Torah and the 5 Megillot and Baer Heitev and the Gemara of Hullin and the laws of Shehitah. The second block in rudimentary handwriting is harder to read. It names 'Ayn Ya'aqov, Pesikta ha-Nasi ha-Gadol, Humash ha-Gadol, and Rav Alfas, and "three excerpts of the Rambam." He signs "I am Men[ah?]em b. Yehudah al-Mujhid (?)." Probably late, at least 16th century. ASE.
Newly treated and encapsulated, must be examined
Newly treated and encapsulated, must be examined
(3r)Tax receipt. Needs examination.
Small fragment with some Judaeo-Arabic text (lā man tawallā. . ."). Unidentified.
Minute blank fragment

Accounts in Arabic script with Greek/Coptic numerals (possibly secondary use). Medieval-era. Along the right margin at 270 degrees, a more faded layer of text is visible in a distinct scribal hand, perhaps fiscal. Requires further examination.

One of the entries reads ورقة من جهة صهري (a document? concerning my brother). Also mentions the price of lead, a lock, and scissors., and the shop.
Literary text, probably. In Arabic script. Contains prayers for Muḥammad and mentions many names. Pinholes at the margin ~4mm apart.

Letter fragment in Judaeo-Arabic. Dating: ca. 11th or 12th century. Wide line spacing. Seems to be a communal letter from an official rebuking a community: קצ . . . ם בהא וכיף מנהאגכם פי אלעמל במק . . . . . גיר מסתתב וסבילכם פי אלעמל בהא גיר מסתקים . . . . אל . . . . . ובנאהם פי כדמתכם . . . . .

Two unrelated fragments. The first is a two-sided fragment of a bifolium of an Arabic medical treatise. The second has three lines in Arabic, probably from a letter. A few loose words from which read as رخام مليح برسم بادهنج "nice marble to structure the windcatcher", and زجاج يكون برسم .... "glass....", last word could be legible and connected to another architectural element. Also mentions "سرعة سرعة", which implies that this could plausibly be a letter fragment. Needs further examination.

Letter from Ibrāhīm b. Abī l-Ḥayy Khalīla to Abū Saʿd Nissim b. Nahray. Ca. 1100. Written after the death of Nahray, hence the estimated dating, concerning the withdrawal of funds from an unspecified business. “Avon” is mentioned; this is probably Avon b. Ṣadaqa, who lived for many years in Jerusalem and, according to this author, has recently arrived in Alexandria. This is the upper fragment.
Newly treated and encapsulated, must be examined

Book list. Most items are volumes of the Talmud. E.g., a commentary on most of Seder Moed by the Ẓarfatiyyim z"l, an Arabic commentary on the Psalms in four bound volumes. Ends with a note regarding a deceased man named Ezra b. Meir.
Legal fragment. In the hand of Ḥalfon b. Menashshe (fl. 1100–1138 CE). Involves a deceased person named Bū l-Riḍā and someone named Elʿazar. There are at least two lines crossed out.

Rental contract. In Hebrew. Dated: Tuesday, 15 Sivan 54[..], so 1640–1739 CE. Location: possibly Cairo, based on the reference to Ḥārat al-Saqāliba in line 4. Sara bt. Yiṣḥaq Malkhī, the widow of Shemuel ha-Levi Kaʿk(?), in the presence of her late husband's son Menaḥem, leases the ʿaliya above the qāʿa where they live to Avraham ha-Kohen b. Yosef for a period of 12 months. The rent is 30 medins per month ('fine and good' ones). Verso: Brief line of writing in pencil, in cursive English: "rest in I." It is unclear why these words would have been recorded as part of any conservation process, wh
List of expenses regarding building according to date? ENA 4047.4 is related.

Letter of complaint, calling on the harassment of Abū l-Najm the filthy "al-Khabīth". Abū l-Najm broke the writer's trust, disobeyed their friendship (lit. sold off their friendship/companionship "abāʿ l-ṣuḥba wa-thiqatahu"), and will be traveling to Damascus. Also mentions Abū l-Faraj the owner of the shop. Regards to his cousin (ibn khālatī) Ibrāhīm and a bunch of other people towards the end.
Newly treated and encapsulated, must be examined

Legal document. The hand of the scribe is probably known (Hillel b. ʿEli?). Fragment (long vertical strip). Involves: [Hiba]tallāh b. Mūsā; a power of attorney; silk; various sums of dinars; a ship; and release formulae.

Legal document. In Arabic script (and language). The handwriting is striking (diwani?). Appears to be dated 8 Ramaḍān 1053 AH, which would be November 1643 CE. There is a symbol of some sort on verso. Needs examination for content.
Newly treated and encapsulated, must be examined
Likely a fiscal account. Needs examination.
Bifolio containing accounts. Late. Listing various numbers.
Legal document acknowledging receipt of 110 dīnārs from the account of ʿArūs b. Yūsuf for a shipment of lac. (information in part from Aodeh.)

Fragment of a quittance document (שטר אביזארי). Written by Hillel b. ʿEli. Location: Fustat. Dated: Wednesday, 15 Ṭevet 4837 AM = 14 December 1076 CE. Given by ʿOvadya b. Fahda to Sālim b. Ṣedaqa ha-Ṣobi (= the Aleppan), through the agent Ṣedaqa b. Moshe, on 6 out of 20 dinars. Signed by Netanʾel b. Yefet, Avraham b. Yefet ha-Levi, Avraham b. Elʿazar ha-Levi, and two different Ṣedaqas. Goitein notes that this is a "Syro-Palestinian group (חבורה)." (Information in part from Goitein's index card.)
Letter from Shemuel b. Hofni, June 977 (Tammuz [1]288 Seleucid).

Recto: Letter in Judaeo-Arabic and Hebrew. Ending only. Some names appear at the bottom: [...] b. Yefet (ZL). And Yefet b. [Yeshuʿa?] ha-Meʿulle ha-Dayyan—this is the writer, as he prefaces his name with 'the one who prays for you.'

tags: Halfon b. Netanel, Letters, trade, aodeh, sugar, gold, IB4, India Book
desc: IB ח98. Verso, with the address on recto: Business letter addressed to Ḥalfon b. Netanʾel ha-Levi. In Arabic script. Dating: Before the beginning of 1136 CE, as that is when Ḥalfon departed Egypt for the west, and when he returned in 1139 CE his brother (here greeted as النازر/al-Nezer) was already dead. Concerning business in goods such as sal ammoniac and turpeth, and mentions a public auction (ḥalqa) several times. (Information in part from Aodeh; see also Hebrew description from Goitein and Friedman, India Book IV.) Ḥalfon reused recto for a draft of a legal document (see separate record).

Legal document mostly in Ladino, with some Hebrew and Aramaic that affirms a transaction for a sum of 100 "pataqas" ("סומה די פטקאס") from Shemuel b. Yiṣḥaq de Ancona and Masʿūd Azulay (l. 1-3r). Location: possibly [Iz]mir, but this reading is tentative in line 14 (איזמיר). The document can be dated to 1772/1773CE through l. 14r 5533 AM. This term "פטקאס" likely indicates coins of Spanish or Austrian mintage, such as a silver real or thaler, that are being sent to Alexandria: "y ditos siyen pataqas me obligo de mandarlos a No Amon [Alexandria]" (l. 3-4r). In lines 10-11r, the document code-swi

Recto: Fragment of a Fatimid state report. Mentions: "the blacks (al-sūdān) and those who accompany them from the nomads (al-jawwāla) and the community (al-jamāʿa). . . the path to corruption in the lands of the sulṭān. . . the slave reported the reason for his patience concerning what they are doing. . . ."
Small fragment of a legal document in the hand of Ḥalfon b. Menashshe ha-Levi (fl. 1100-1138 CE). Involving a woman and her ketubba conditions. No names.

Legal document. The bottom part of a quittance from Fusṭāṭ, ca 1150s, in which the trader Abū l-Maʿālī Shemuʾel b. Yehuda Ibn Asad is released from any further obligation or debt by Sumr bt. Moshe and her son Abū l-Ḥasan. Because of debts that Sumr's late husband owed, she and her children hid from debt collectors in Shemuʾel's home until he settled the debts for them. This is a court record, and it is signed by Mevōrakh b. Natan he-Ḥaver (fl. 1150–1181 CE) and Yeḥezqel b. Natan, with the validation of Ḥiyya b. Yiṣḥaq, Efrayim b. Meshullam, and Hillel b. Letter from "Sāsī" to R. D[...]. In Judaeo-Arabic. Dating: After 1517 CE (uses the term 'basha' twice), but not long after (Avraham Castro appears in the letter). Dealing with business matters. Complaining about someone who mistreated the writer. Mentions Avraham Castro; Ibrāhīm al-Kalaḥ; Mūsā Ḥaqqān. Mentions taxes incumbent on "all who arrive from Hind and Sind and the lands of the Arabs," more than the tithe (ʿushr).
